summary: Edith Wyschogrod worked in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Hunter College (~1953–1957) and Columbia University (~1965–1970). She served on the faculty at Rice University from around 1992 to 2003 and taught Lucy Annette Jones.
Edmond Yee is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. Around 1982, he held faculty posts at Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union. He also taught Heng Sure.

Edmund Hardy was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and religious studies specialist. He studied at Heidelberg University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Freiburg (1885–1893) and held a professorship at Fribourg (1893–1898).

Edmund Leach worked in religious studies. He studied at Clare College, King's College, and the London School of Economics, also studying under Bronislaw Malinowski (~1937–1939). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1953 to 1979.
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indology scholar. He graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University (~1882–1886) and studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg from circa 1886 to 1889.

Edo Shonin works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He has served as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and as Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Eduard Hermann specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying under Berthold Delbrück (~1891–1893). He held academic posts at the University of Kiel (~1913–1917), Goethe University Frankfurt (~1917–1924), and the University of Göttingen (~1924–1937).

Eduard Müller was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his Inauguraldissertation at Leipzig University (~1871–1874) and served as a professor at the University of Bern from around 1887 to 1908.

Eduard Sachau worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He studied at Kiel and Leipzig, learning under Hermann Brockhaus. He held posts at Vienna, Frederick William University Berlin, Humboldt University, and directed the Seminar for Oriental Languages.

Eduard Sievers was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University and Frederick William University Berlin. He served as a professor at the University of Jena (1871–1883) and held posts at Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leipzig.

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (~2013–2014), where he was supervised by Y. Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.
Edward Albert Gait was an Indologist and historian. He studied at University College London until circa 1882 and founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Charterhouse School and Merton College, he served as Professor of Hindústání at East India Company College (~1845–1857) and at the Foreign Office.

Edward Byles Cowell studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and Sanskrit College before serving as Professor at the University of Cambridge (1867–1903).
Edward C. Dimock was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Yale University from circa 1950 to 1953 and held a post at the University of Chicago from around 1957 to 1992.
Edward Clive Bayley specialized in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Haileybury and the East India Company College (~1840–1842) before joining the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Edward Conze worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his Ph.D. at Cologne and studying at Bonn. He held posts at the University of London, the Buddhist Society, the University of Washington, UC Berkeley, and Lancaster University.

Edward Denison Ross was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and history. He studied at University College London, later holding posts there, at the British Museum, and as head of SOAS University of London (~1916–1937).

Edward Elbridge Salisbury studied at Yale and under scholars including Woolsey, de Sacy, de Tassy, Bopp, Burnouf, and Lassen. An Indologist and linguist, he served as Professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale University (1841–1854).
Edward Espe Brown is a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied under Shunryu Suzuki from circa 1966 to 1971, as well as under Reb Anderson and Jack Kornfield.
